subject: Private deployment license exception + evidence roadmap
messages:
From: Lena Brooks <lena.brooks@greenvalleymed.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@greenvalleymed.com
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private hosting request + redlines (GVM)

Hi Sean —

Thanks for running through the solution last week. Following internal review, Green Valley Medical Center wants to move forward with a private (on‑prem) deployment in our primary data center. A few legal/procurement asks came back that we'll need to resolve before procurement will sign the order form:

1) License scope: we need explicit language allowing use of the runtime for PHI processing within our environments and a carveout that prevents Redwood from asserting remote access rights except for narrowly scoped witness/audit windows.
2) Evidence/escrow: GVM cannot accept full custody transfer of keys. We would like an escrow‑like arrangement (signed attestation + sealed image snapshot transfer) or a witnessless proof of access routine that satisfies our compliance team.
3) Audit windows: specify maximum duration and notice requirements for any on‑site or remote audit.
4) SLA addendum: uptime and recovery objectives for the dedicated cluster and proof of restoration runbooks.

Attached are our standard security checklist and our marked redlines to the MSA and order form. Can you loop in legal and operations and confirm what exceptions Redwood can accept? Procurement needs final language or a short memo that we can attach to the PO by 12/10.

Attachments: GVM-DA-2026-Security-Checklist.pdf; Redlines_MSA_2026.docx

Best,
Lena Brooks
Director, IT Procurement
Green Valley Medical Center
procurement@greenvalleymed.com
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lena Brooks <lena.brooks@greenvalleymed.com>
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Private hosting request + redlines (GVM)

Lena — thanks for the clear list and the redlines. I’ve copied Neha (legal) and Marissa (solutions) so we can triage quickly. High level response:

- License scope: open to adding explicit PHI runtime use wording and to narrow Redwood’s remote access rights.
- Evidence/escrow: we cannot hand over customer keys. We can propose a sealed snapshot + notarized attestation workflow; Neha will propose exact wording.
- Audit windows: we can limit to two site windows per year + remote evidence requests with 48h notice; will confirm.
- SLA: we'll draft an appendix with RTO/RPO targets for the dedicated cluster.

Can we schedule a 30‑minute legal/ops call tomorrow or Thursday to resolve the remaining redlines? Suggested times: Wed 12/02 11:00–11:30 PT or Thu 12/03 09:00–09:30 PT.

I’ll follow up with a short proposal and the annex draft.

Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Lena Brooks <lena.brooks@greenvalleymed.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 13:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Private hosting request + redlines (GVM) — proposed legal approach

Lena / Sean — quick legal take after initial review of the redlines you sent. We prefer to avoid language that obligates Redwood to transfer cryptographic keys or otherwise create a custody obligation. That said, there are pragmatic compromises that generally satisfy health‑system compliance teams: 

Proposed compromise (short form):
- Runtime license: add a limited license grant in the Annex that permits GVM to run a hardware‑bound instance of the runtime with PHI processing rights for the term of the Order Form; restrict redistribution/third‑party sublicensing.
- Witnessless sealed snapshot: Redwood will produce a signed, time‑stamped disk image and an attestation of the build (hashes, build manifest). The image will be encrypted; Redwood will deposit the encryption key with a mutually agreed third‑party escrow (or KMS escrow service) under specified release conditions (e.g., insolvency, contract termination after cure period). The escrow arrangement will be documented in Exhibit B.
- Operator access: Redwood will accept a narrow operator access carveout limited to pre‑scheduled, observable remediation windows with a max duration (e.g., 4 hours) and written notice. Any tooling access will be read‑only unless explicitly authorized.
- Audit windows: define notice (48–72 hours depending on on‑site vs remote), max duration (on‑site: 2 business days; remote: 4 hours), and scope (logs, manifests, attestation verification). Redactions for third‑party data will be allowed.
- SLA appendix: add RTO/RPO and a runbook validation clause (quarterly restoration drills with customer witness option).

I’ve drafted language for Exhibit B (attached as Proposed_Annex_escrow.txt). If GVM can accept the escrow‑trigger conditions and the limitation on key custody, I think this will be workable. If they insist on direct key handback outside of insolvency/termination triggers, we’ll need exec signoff.

Next steps: Sean — if you can get procurement to accept the escrow triggers, Marissa and I will turn this into track‑changes and an Annex for the MSA/order form.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Sr. Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
Attachment: Proposed_Annex_escrow.txt
From: Kyle Morgan <kyle.morgan@greenvalleymed.com>
To: neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com, sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Lena Brooks <lena.brooks@greenvalleymed.com>, procurement@greenvalleymed.com
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 08:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Private hosting request + redlines (GVM) — procurement questions

Hi Neha / Sean —

Thanks for the thoughtful proposal. Procurement has two follow ups before we can present this to the approvals board: 

1) Can you confirm the identity of the third‑party escrow provider (or categories of providers) you are willing to use? We prefer a vendor with SOC 2 and SSAE attestations.
2) For the sealed snapshot workflow, we need an integrity verification procedure that our security team can run (hash list + verification steps). Please attach a one‑page verification checklist that we can hand to our sysadmin.

Also: procurement will want the SLA draft as a separate PDF we can include in the PO. If you can send the Annex with track changes and a sample verification checklist by EOD Friday 12/04, that will keep us on the 12/10 signoff timeline.

Thanks,
Kyle Morgan
Sr. Procurement Manager
Green Valley Medical Center
procurement@greenvalleymed.com
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lena Brooks <lena.brooks@greenvalleymed.com>, Kyle Morgan <kyle.morgan@greenvalleymed.com>
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 16:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Private hosting request + redlines (GVM) — next steps and deliverables

Kyle / Lena —

Summary / next steps from our side:
- Neha will finalize the Exhibit B escrow language and the sealed snapshot attestation by EOD Friday 12/04 (attached: Proposed_Annex_escrow.txt).
- Marissa will produce a one‑page verification checklist and an SLA appendix PDF (SLA-draft-privdeploy.pdf).
- Redwood is prepared to use a SOC‑2 compliant escrow provider (we commonly use IronBound Escrow or Custodia KMS services; we'll include options and references).
- Proposed call to walk procurement/security through the verification steps: Mon 12/07 10:00–10:30 PT. Let me know if that works.

If procurement is comfortable with the escrow trigger conditions (insolvency, contract termination post‑cure, or court order with protections), we do not need executive signoff. If they require unconditional key handback on termination, that will be an escalation to our General Counsel.

I'll attach the documents as promised in a follow‑up email and share a HubSpot deal record link so you can reference the redline versions.

Thanks —
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
Attachments (referenced): Proposed_Annex_escrow.txt; SLA-draft-privdeploy.pdf
